newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says no preconditions to talks with Syria.
newsitem.headline: Israel says no preconditions to talks with Syria.

text.p: Israel said on Saturday it had no preconditions in order to resume peace negotiations with Syria, said Eliyahu Ben Elissar, Israel's new Ambassador to the United States.

But in an interview with Israel Television Channel One Ben Elissar, who would head an Israeli team if there were talks with Syria, evaded questions on whether Israel would be willing to cede the Golan Heights, a Syrian condition for the renewal of talks.

Peace negotiations between Israel and Syria stalled before the May election of right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Netanyahu ran on a pledge not to return the strategic plateau captured from Syria in the 1967 Arab-Israeli War.
Asked if a pullback from the Golan was no longer a condition of Prime Minister Netanyahu, Ben Elissar said: "Everything we have to say will be said at the negotiating table."

"We never said we are placing preconditions to conduct negotiations with the Syrians. We always said that we are requesting to hold talks, hold negotiations and that all sides would be able to present their positions at the negotiating table."
